title: VPN Connected Users and the VPN Diagnostics pages: user logs, traffic flow logs and access policy data

prose.text: {{connected-users}} The vpnConnectedUsers API read is in [[zpa.api.machine-groups-wire]].

prose.label: Streamed VPN logs.
prose.text: {{connection-id-merge}} The streamed Traffic Flow VPN page's field table and example record differ on its time fields and session state {{divergence:traffic-flow-vpn-example}}.

prose.label: Open.
prose.text: The time ranges, retention and export limits of these pages are open {{gap:ranges-retention}}, as are the values of some fields {{gap:field-values}} and whether these console fields are the streamed ones {{gap:lss-relation}}.

The streamed log types are in [[zpa.log-receivers.log-types]]; the User Activity Diagnostics pages are in [[zpa.troubleshooting.diagnostics]] and [[zpa.troubleshooting.user-activity-diagnostics]]; remote commands are in [[zpa.vpn.support-information]]; the hub is [[zpa.vpn]].

connected-users.statement: The VPN Connected Users page shows a user's connection status to a VPN Service Edge, and displays the username, assigned client IP address, connected VPN Service Edge and the current VPN connection status. Username is the user's email address, Client IP Address is the address assigned to the client, Hostname is the client's hostname, and Connected Device State indicates whether the client device is connected or disconnected from the VPN Service Edge.

quotes: The VPN Connected Users page shows a user's connection status to a VPN Service Edge. It also displays the username, assigned client IP address, connected VPN Service Edge, and the current VPN connection status.
Username: The email address of the user.
Client IP Address: The IP address assigned to the client.
Hostname: The hostname of the client.
Connected Device State: Indicates if the client device is connected or disconnected from the VPN Service Edge.

user-logs-counters.statement: The User Logs page of VPN Diagnostics shows the number of Total, Successful, Errors and Others transactions for users' VPN connections.

quotes: View the number of Total, Successful, Errors, and Others transactions for users' VPN connections.

user-logs-fields.statement: A user log entry has an Event Type (the type of VPN session event), a Connection End (blank if the VPN connection is ongoing), a Client Name (the client's email address), a Result (Success or Error) and a Client Tunnel IP. Its details include the Client Version (the Client Connector version), the Last Handshake (date and time of the last TCP handshake), the ZPA Service Edge, a Failure Reason, the VPN Service Edge IP and a Connection ID.

quotes: Event Type: The type of VPN session event for the user.
Connection End: The day and time when the VPN session ended. This field is blank if the VPN connection is ongoing.
Client Name: The email address of the client who initiated the VPN session.
Result: The result of the VPN session (Success or Error).
Client Tunnel IP: The IP address of the tunnel through which the user's traffic is forwarded.
Client Version: The Zscaler Client Connector version running on the user's device.
Last Handshake: The date and time of the last TCP handshake.
ZPA Service Edge: The Private Access Service Edge for the connection.
Failure Reason: The reason for VPN connection failure, if failed.
VPN Service Edge IP: The IP address of the VPN Service Edge that carried the traffic.
Connection ID: The unique ID assigned to identify the connection.

traffic-flow-fields.statement: A traffic flow log entry has a Session State (Open or Closed), a Source and a Destination (IP address and port number) and a Protocol (TCP or UDP). Its details include the Access Policy triggered by the traffic, the Duration the connection was active, and the total bytes and packets received and sent.

quotes: Session State: The current traffic session state (Open or Closed).
Source: The IP address and the port number from where the traffic originated.
Destination: The destination IP address and the port number for the traffic.
Protocol: The protocol for the traffic (TCP or UDP).
Access Policy: The name of the access policy triggered by the traffic.
Duration: The duration that the connection was active.
Total Byte Received: The bytes of data received by the client during the session.
Total Byte Sent: The bytes of data sent during the session.
Total Packet Received: The number of packets received by the client during the session.
Total Packet Sent: The number of packets sent during the session.

connection-id-merge.statement: The User Status - VPN Service Edge and User Status - VPN Service Edge (IP Address Reservation) log types share a ConnectionID key field, which can be used to merge the user status logs produced by both, and which enables SIEM servers to link, correlate and integrate the data from both sources.

quotes: You can use the shared ConnectionID key field to merge user status logs produced by both VPN Service Edge and VPN Service Edge (IP Address Reservation).
This common identifier enables SIEM servers to effectively link, correlate, and integrate the data from both sources.
You can use the shared ConnectionID key field to merge user status logs produced by both User Status - VPN Service Edge (IP Address Reservation) and VPN Service Edge.

log-export.statement: The user logs and the traffic logs can each be viewed in JSON format or downloaded as a text file.

quotes: View the user logs in JSON format.
Download the user logs as a text file.
View the traffic logs in JSON format.
Download the traffic logs as a text file.

access-policy-data.statement: On the Access Policy Data page the VPN Service Edge to view is selected, and the page shows the total bytes and packets allowed and blocked for users' VPN connections, including traffic that does not match any access policy rule and is blocked by default. Each rule shows Bytes and Packets, and the policy rule history drawer has Bytes and Packets charts for all the traffic that triggered the rule.

quotes: Traffic that does not match any access policy rules is blocked by default, and you can also view that data on this page.
Select the VPN Service Edge you want to view the data for.
View the number of total bytes allowed and blocked for users' VPN connections.
View the number of total packets allowed and blocked for users' VPN connections.
Bytes: The bytes of the data handled during the session.
Packets: The number of packets exchanged during the session.

The policy rule history drawer contains two charts, Bytes and Packets, showing the bytes of data and the number of packets transferred by all the traffic that triggered the access policy rule, respectively.

traffic-flow-vpn-example.summary: On the Traffic Flow for VPN (For Legacy Apps) log fields page, the table gives FlowStartTime integer and float format specifiers and describes SessionState as open or closed, while the example record writes FlowStartTime as an ISO date string and SessionState as "close".

quotes: | FlowStartTime | The time when the traffic flow started | %[OPT]d %[OPT]x %[OPT]f %[OPT]o |
| SessionState | The state of the traffic flow session (e.g., open or closed) | %[OPT]s %[OPT]j %[OPT]J %[OPT]o |

positions.says: Table: FlowStartTime takes the integer and float specifiers %[OPT]d, %[OPT]x, %[OPT]f and %[OPT]o, and SessionState is described as open or closed.

quotes: "SessionState": "close"

positions.says: Example record: FlowStartTime is an ISO date string and SessionState is "close".

traffic-flow-vpn-example.impact: A consumer cannot tell from the article whether FlowStartTime is numeric or a date string, or whether SessionState takes open and closed or "close".

ranges-retention.title: Time ranges, retention and export limits of the VPN Diagnostics pages
ranges-retention.detail: The User Logs, Traffic Flow Logs and Access Policy Data pages as captured give no time range presets, default range, retention or export limits.

field-values.title: The values of Event Type, Failure Reason and the Others transaction class
field-values.detail: The captured pages name the Event Type and Failure Reason fields and the Others counter without listing their values or defining the Others class.

lss-relation.title: Whether the console diagnostics fields are the streamed VPN log fields
lss-relation.detail: Three captures outside this area hold the streamed counterparts (the User Status VPN Service Edge, its IP Address Reservation and the Traffic Flow VPN log fields), and no page says whether the console fields above are those fields.
